- Overestimate prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon when sentiment is bullish (sentiment > 0.5) and understate when sentiment is bearish (sentiment < 0.3).  
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- Underestimate late-period (last 7–10 days) prices when sentiment is consistently bullish; model tends to lag in recognizing sustained momentum.  
- Mean-revert mid-horizon forecasts if sentiment oscillates between 0.27–0.53; avoid prolonged upward drift without strong sentiment support.  
- When sentiment is low (0.0–0.27), model often underestimates true price, so add 2–5% to forecast to account for hidden risk premium or market resilience.
